MD-2026-HB1101.s: In Worcester County, the law creates a temporary permit that can let certain beer, wine, and liquor license holders sell drinks to go during a special event. It also creates a Class C per diem municipal to-go license, which a municipality can get for a special event area. The county board must adopt rules for these permits and licenses.

MD-2026-HB1110.s: The law changes notice rules when a county or town files a court case to foreclose on certain vacant and abandoned property over unpaid taxes. Instead of sending notice by first-class and certified mail, the complaint must be served on each interested party under Maryland court rules. It takes effect June 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB1148.s: The law creates an Heirs Legacy Protection Program to help heirs who inherit a home become the record owner, stay in the home, and avoid tax sales. It also expands the State Tax Sale Ombudsman’s help to include people acting for a deceased homeowner or an heir, and it sets up a fund for the program. The law also lets some heirs qualify for homeowner and homestead tax credits even if the deed is not yet in their name, if they meet other rules.

MD-2026-HB1151.s: The bill would require the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to study whether Medicaid should pay for room and board at hospice houses. The study would look at costs, savings, hospital stays, emergency room use, and how other states handle this payment. The department would report its findings to the House Health Committee and Senate Finance Committee by December 1, 2026, and the act would take effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB121.s: In Baltimore County, this law lets certain restaurants and bars with Class B or Class D licenses apply to sell mixed drinks and cocktails for takeout if the county licensing board adopts rules first. The drink must be bought with prepared food, the buyer must be 21 or older with valid ID, and the drink must be in a sealed container and sold by 11 p.m. The board may not charge an extra fee for this, may set a limit on how much one person can buy in one sale, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB1335.s: The law requires the Department of Information Technology to hire a third party to study state staffing and skills needs for information technology and cybersecurity jobs. The study must look at current positions, gaps in needed skills, pay comparisons, and ways to improve hiring and retention for state tech workers. The department must send the study to the Governor and the General Assembly by November 1, 2027; the law takes effect July 1, 2026, and ends June 30, 2028.

MD-2026-HB1434.s: The Maryland Department of Health would have to create and keep up a central webpage for caregivers in the state. The page would give plain-language help and links about care for children with special health needs, adults with disabilities or illness, older adults, caregiver health, local programs, safety planning, and data privacy and security. It would take effect October 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB1457.s: The law lets the circuit administrative judge for the Fourth Circuit set up a truancy reduction pilot program in the juvenile court in Washington County. It also lets the state chief justice accept gifts or grants to help run these pilot programs. The law takes effect October 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB1474.s: In Baltimore County, this law changes when some alcohol licenses can be moved to a different area or changed to a different type. It lets the county board approve limited transfers of some Class B and Class D licenses, and some transferred Class D licenses must become Class B licenses. It also removes older special rules for some Towson and Hunt Valley license transfers and conversions.

MD-2026-HB1526.s: In Carroll County, the bill creates a new permit for Class 1 distilleries to sell, prepare, and serve food, nonalcoholic drinks, and certain alcoholic drinks for people drinking on site. It also lets these distilleries use their licensed space for events, with health department approval needed for food and drink service. The county licensing board may issue the permit and set a yearly fee. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB168.s: The law lets county school boards treat educator workforce housing as a school purpose and allows state housing help to be used for it. It defines this housing as affordable homes set aside for teachers and other local school staff, and says those workers can count as a special group for some federal housing tax credit rules. It also expands a state housing loan fund to local housing authorities, counties, municipal corporations, and school boards for mixed-income housing and educator housing.

MD-2026-HB2100.s: This measure would amend the Maryland Constitution to say that the district rules in it apply only to districts for the state Senate and House of Delegates. It would also let the General Assembly give the Supreme Court of Maryland original power to review the state’s congressional district plan, and it says the Constitution itself does not set the rules for congressional district lines. The change would go to voters at the November 2026 general election.

MD-2026-HB2101.s: The bill would withdraw and repeal sections 2 through 4 of Chapter 156 of 2026, which dealt with a duplicate proposed constitutional amendment on collective bargaining for state employees. It also makes a change to section 5 of that law. The act is an emergency measure and took effect when it was signed into law on August 5, 2026.

MD-2026-HB2102.s: The bill would change Maryland’s Constitution to require each House of Delegates district to be split into three single-member delegate districts. It would also create a new redistricting convention to draw both state and congressional district maps after each census. If the convention approves a plan, it could become law unless the General Assembly challenges it and the Supreme Court of Maryland rejects it.

MD-2026-HB211.s: Baltimore County may grant a property tax credit for real property owned by Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 at 730 Wampler Road in Middle River. The credit would cover 100% of the county property tax on that property. The law takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.

MD-2026-HB311.s: The bill requires each local school system to look for accessibility problems for students with disabilities when it does safety checks of schools. It also requires annual reports to include cases where a school became hard to access in a way that could affect evacuation or emergency response, and it makes those reports confidential except for members of the General Assembly who request them. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB406.s: In Prince George’s County, the bill changes the rules on holding more than one alcohol license. It adds Class B on-sale beer and wine licenses and Class B on-sale beer, wine, and liquor licenses to the list of licenses that can be held even when the usual one-license limit would apply. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB443.s: The law creates a new beer, wine, and liquor license for small event centers in Prince George’s County. It lets the county license board issue the permit to certain venues with kitchen and dining space for 75 to 125 people, and it sets limits on how many can be issued. The annual fee is $3,500, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB456.s: In Howard County, the law creates a gift basket permit for certain flower and gift basket businesses. The permit lets them sell and deliver gift baskets with limited amounts of beer, wine, or liquor to adults 21 and older, and the permit fee is $100. It takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB457.s: The law requires colleges and universities in Maryland that have on-campus housing to provide free menstrual hygiene products, like tampons or sanitary pads, in restrooms and student health centers. It applies to institutions of higher education with on-campus housing. The law takes effect July 1, 2026, and the products must be provided by August 1, 2028.

MD-2026-HB529.s: The bill updates and reorganizes Maryland’s laws for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, which is the state Medicaid program. It renumbers and rewrites several sections of the health code and adds some new sections for that program. The bill was enacted as Chapter 865.

MD-2026-HB558.s: The bill changes wine festival licenses in Prince George’s County. It removes the yearly limit on how many of these licenses the local board may issue and drops the ban on using one in a certain legislative district. It also lets the board choose the festival location and dates each year within set limits, and it takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB583.s: In Prince George’s County, this law updates the office name that must get notice when a Class C per diem beer, wine, and liquor license is issued. The notice goes to the county police chief, county fire chief, the Department of Permitting, Inspections, and Enforcement, and, if needed, the local town or city leader. It takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB664.s: The law changes how many Class A alcohol licenses Cecil County may issue. It ties the limit to a set number of registered voters and says at least two Class A licenses must be allowed in each election district. It takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB711.s: The law tightens rules on how some companies and agencies handle personal data. It bars selling a consumer’s data for immigration enforcement in certain cases, adds limits for public records, and requires some systems that switch messages to set rules for system access. It also expands what counts as sensitive data, including things like health, race, religion, immigration status, and precise location.

MD-2026-HB727.s: The bill changes who can join a veterans’ organization in Anne Arundel County for a Class C liquor license. It would let certain members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service count, and it would remove the rule that members had to have served in a war. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB776.s: The law requires juvenile intake officers to file a supervision petition when a child under 13 is alleged to have done an act that caused a victim’s death. It also requires police to send that kind of complaint to the Department of Juvenile Services for action. The law takes effect October 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB783.s: In Washington County, local governments would have to give a 100% property tax credit on certain real estate owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated. The property must be used to provide housing for veterans. The law takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to tax years beginning after June 30, 2026.

MD-2026-HB845.s: The law expands Maryland’s scholarship aid for higher education. It lets certain Delmar, Maryland residents who graduated from Delmar High School in Delaware qualify for the Community College Promise Scholarship, and it broadens the transportation workers scholarship to cover some surviving workers and family members. It also renames that program and lets its scholarship pay for the full cost of attending a college or university.

MD-2026-HB846.s: The law exempts certain property from property tax if it is owned by the City of Hagerstown or the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc. and is used mainly for public social, recreation, and entertainment uses. The tax break also applies back to tax years starting after June 30, 2023, and the State, Washington County, and the city must refund any extra tax paid because of it. The act takes effect June 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB862.s: The law would require freight trains in Maryland to have at least two crew members when they run on the same rail corridor as a high-speed passenger or commuter train, with some yard-service work excluded. A railroad company could face a civil fine of up to $10,000, or up to $25,000 for a repeat willful violation within three years. The rule would take effect only if similar laws are passed in New York, Pennsylvania, and Virginia, and if that happens by October 1, 2056; otherwise, it would not take effect.

MD-2026-HB889.s: In Wicomico County, local leaders may give a property tax credit for certain real estate owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc. The property must be used to develop, fix up, and transfer homes to private owners, and it cannot be admin or warehouse buildings. If a credit is granted, the group must send a yearly report on its property holdings and transactions there. The law takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to tax years starting after June 30, 2026.

MD-2026-HB914.s: The law increases Worcester County’s Board of License Commissioners from three members to five. It also sets the start dates for the two new members and keeps the current members’ term end dates in place. The law takes effect June 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB929.s: In Carroll County, the permits office may deny or renew a commercial license or permit if the applicant has unpaid personal property taxes. If the applicant shows the taxes are being disputed, the office may not deny the license or permit for that reason. The office may also issue or renew the license or permit once the unpaid taxes are paid. The law takes effect October 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB936.s: In Montgomery County, the public school system must identify and post on its website how much food it bought for school meals from certified local farms and certified Chesapeake invasive species providers in the 2026–2027 school year. It must also set target increases for those purchases for later school years and make a plan, with the Office of Food Systems Resilience and public input, to meet those targets. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB991.s: The law changes the hours when Harford County health clubs with a Class HC beer and wine license may sell beer and wine for drinking on site. The sale window is extended from 1 p.m. to 9 p.m. to 1 p.m. to 11 p.m. It took effect on July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB148.s: The law creates a state income tax credit for retired 9-1-1 specialists, starting with tax years after December 31, 2025 and before January 1, 2029. The credit is worth 4.75% of the first $15,000 of certain retirement income, up to $700 a year, and the total credits statewide cannot exceed $250,000 each year. The Department of Emergency Management must also report on the credits it gives out and on 9-1-1 specialists who have vested in a retirement system.

MD-2026-SB16.s: The law limits how much can be taken from a person’s pay for child support in some cases, especially when the person’s income is at or below 250% of the federal poverty level. It also requires employer notices to explain these limits and lets an employee challenge a withholding if it goes over the allowed amount. The changes affect child support obligors, their employers, and employees who get a withholding notice. It takes effect October 1, 2028.

MD-2026-SB2100.s: This proposed constitutional amendment would say that Maryland’s redistricting rules for compact, adjoining, equal-population districts apply only to the State Senate and House of Delegates. It would also let the General Assembly give the Supreme Court of Maryland power to review the state’s congressional district map. The change would go to voters at the November 2026 general election.

MD-2026-SB2101.s: The bill would withdraw and repeal a duplicate proposed constitutional amendment tied to collective bargaining for state employees. It would remove and repeal Sections 2 through 4 of Chapter 156 of the Acts of 2026, and it is linked to another constitutional amendment that must pass and be approved by voters. It is an emergency measure and would take effect when enacted.

MD-2026-SB2102.s: The bill would change Maryland’s constitution to require each legislative district to be split into three single-member delegate districts, where one delegate is elected from each area. It would set new rules for drawing both state and congressional districts, including keeping them compact, connected, and fair to communities, and not using voter party or past votes. It would also create an independent redistricting commission, give the state Supreme Court power to set district maps if needed, and change some Attorney General duties tied to those cases.

MD-2026-SB244.s: The law updates and reorganizes Maryland’s rules for the Medical Assistance Program, which is the state Medicaid program. It renumbers some sections, revises older text, and adds new sections to the health code. It also keeps in place the program’s rules on who can get covered health care services and some specific benefits.

MD-2026-SB311.s: The bill changes parts of Maryland’s Blueprint for Maryland’s Future. It would remove a yearly school technology report, extend some school funding and dual-enrollment time limits, change rules for teacher and principal certification, and update several career and technical education and school support programs. It also would change how some education funds and low-income student counts are handled for state funding formulas.

MD-2026-SB322.s: The law changes when a person with a criminal conviction can be kept off a jury in Maryland. It says a person is not qualified if they are still serving a sentence, including parole or probation, for certain crimes, or if they were convicted of perjury, witness intimidation, jury intimidation, or a crime under Title 8 of the Criminal Law Article. It also keeps people with pending charges for a crime punishable by more than 1 year in prison from serving, and it takes effect October 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB366.s: Enacted in Maryland, this law creates a pilot program for certain drivers whose licenses would be suspended or revoked because of point totals from serious traffic violations, including speeding, reckless driving, or racing. The Motor Vehicle Administration must give these participants a restricted license that requires an intelligent speed assistance system, which is a device that helps keep a car from going over the speed limit. The agency must set a fee to cover program costs, waive it for indigent people, and limit how data from the program can be used and shared.

MD-2026-SB396.s: The law raises the minimum and maximum salary range for the chief inspector who works for the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners. It affects that one county job in the board that handles alcoholic beverage licenses. The change takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB399.s: In Anne Arundel County, this law changes the daily fee setup for certain short-term alcohol licenses used for events. For events with fewer than 500 people, the fee is $25 a day for beer or beer-and-wine licenses and $50 a day for beer, wine, and liquor licenses. For events with 500 or more people, those fees are charged per alcohol-selling point of sale at the event each day. It takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB400.s: The law changes entertainment permits for certain alcohol license holders in Anne Arundel County. It renames some permits, changes what kinds of music, TV, karaoke, trivia, dancing, and other entertainment are allowed, and adds a rule that outdoor events must be at least 100 feet from residentially zoned property in some cases. It also changes permit fees and takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB401.s: The bill raises the annual pay for the chair and other members of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners, and it adds cost-of-living raises tied to county employees. It also raises pay for part-time inspectors and keeps a monthly expense allowance for each inspector. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB426.s: The law makes most records tied to a divorce case closed to public view. It covers items like divorce applications, financial records, settlement records, and custody orders, but not the final divorce decree. The records may still be released to the people involved, their lawyers, or anyone allowed by a court order. It took effect October 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB441.s: The law creates a new golf course liquor license in Anne Arundel County for golf courses with at least nine holes, letting the holder sell beer, wine, and liquor for drinking on site. It also creates sports activity venue licenses for places like bowling centers, golf simulators, pickleball courts, gyms, and similar sites, with rules for where alcohol can be sold, food service, staff training, and crowd control. The law takes effect July 1, 2026, and sets annual fees of $740 or $1,200 for the sports venue licenses, and $1,200 for the golf course license.

MD-2026-SB442.s: The bill creates an exemption from Anne Arundel County’s population cap for certain Class A and Class D off-sale alcohol licenses. It lets the county board approve some licenses even if the number of off-sale licenses in an assessment district is over the usual limit, including certain applications filed on or after January 1, 2023 and approved before July 1, 2025. The act takes effect July 1, 2026, and was approved by the Governor on May 26, 2026.

MD-2026-SB448.s: The bill would let Carroll County borrow up to $27 million for public facilities, including water and sewer projects, roads, bridges, schools, county buildings, and parks. It would also let the county make loans to volunteer fire departments for equipment, buildings, and other related needs, and use some borrowing to buy farm or woodland easements. The county would have to repay the bonds with property taxes, and the bond income would be exempt from Maryland taxes.

MD-2026-SB450.s: In Carroll County, the permits office may deny or renew a commercial license or permit if the applicant has unpaid personal property taxes. It may not do that if the applicant shows the taxes are being disputed, and it may issue or renew the permit once the unpaid taxes are paid. The law takes effect October 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB459.s: State agencies would have to aim for 50% of their spending on print and digital ads to go directly to local Maryland news organizations. The bill sets rules for which news groups count, including some print, digital, nonprofit, and broadcast outlets, and lets agencies work with a nonprofit to keep a list of eligible groups. It would take effect October 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB48.s: The law changes how Maryland reviews public school construction projects. It raises some approval dollar limits, lets the school construction commission set rules for state funding, and requires an appeal process and more reports to counties and local governments. It also changes when the state can ask counties to pay back debt on old school buildings and updates how school building maintenance and safety reviews are done.

MD-2026-SB497.s: The bill exempts from property tax certain property owned by the City of Hagerstown or the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc. The property must be used mainly for public social, recreation, and entertainment uses. It also makes the exemption apply back to tax years starting after June 30, 2023, and requires refunds for excess tax paid because of that change. The act takes effect June 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB501.s: Washington County and its towns would have to give a 100% property tax credit on certain real estate owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated and used to house veterans. The credit would apply to county and municipal property taxes. The law takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.

MD-2026-SB524.s: The law lets certain Baltimore City Mayor’s offices get juvenile police and court records when they are helping a child with programs and services. Before getting the records, the office must sign a written agreement and get written consent from the child’s parent or guardian. The offices must keep the records private and can be held responsible if they share them without permission.

MD-2026-SB529.s: The law creates a Southern Maryland early college teacher pathway program for high school students. It lets students begin teacher prep work for primary and secondary schools, and says they cannot be charged tuition or mandatory fees for the program. It also sets up a workgroup to develop recommendations for the program and a teacher prep path in Southern Maryland, with members from state, college, county, and local school groups in Calvert, Charles, and St. Mary’s counties.

MD-2026-SB532.s: Public senior colleges and community colleges in Maryland would have to report each year on how students can get over-the-counter birth control on campus. Community colleges would also have to give students access to all types of over-the-counter contraception, such as through a health center, campus stores, vending machines, or another way that works on campus. The reports would go to the Maryland Higher Education Commission, which would send a yearly report to lawmakers. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB636.s: In Baltimore City, the law changes some rules for certain alcohol license holders. It removes a September 30 deadline for paying a $120 fee to use Sunday sales hours for Class A beer and light wine and Class A beer, wine, and liquor licenses. It also changes the tax proof deadline to March 30 each year for renewal licenses, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB646.s: The law bars public school system contracts from including certain terms, such as binding arbitration, forced payment without funds, automatic renewal, or limits on getting legal help. If one of those terms is put in a contract, it is void, and the rest of the contract can still be enforced. It applies to contracts signed on or after July 1, 2026, and not to earlier contracts or their renewal or extension.

MD-2026-SB700.s: In Wicomico County, this law changes the sale hours for a Class B beer, wine, and liquor golf course license. License holders may sell from 7 a.m. to 2 a.m. Monday through Saturday, and from 7 a.m. to midnight on Sunday. It takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB709.s: The bill would create a Purple Star Colleges Program to recognize colleges that give strong support to military-connected students. The Maryland Higher Education Commission would run the program and set the rules for a college to qualify, including naming a staff contact, posting a student resource page, keeping a transition program, and giving staff training. It would also update the definition of “military-connected student” in the existing Purple Star Schools Program. The act takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB715.s: The bill lets the Circuit Administrative Judge in Washington County set up a truancy reduction pilot program in juvenile court. It also lets the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland accept gifts or grants to help run the pilot programs. The law takes effect October 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB776.s: The bill creates a Maryland commission to study the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children. It would look into the history of the site, the deaths of children buried there, and the condition of the cemetery, and it would help identify remains, notify descendants, and consider a memorial and other steps for healing and reform. The law was approved by the governor on May 26, 2026.

MD-2026-SB791.s: The law limits how state and local correctional facilities and law enforcement can work with federal immigration authorities. It bars many checks, holds, transfers, and threats based on a person’s immigration status, with some exceptions, and it requires state facilities to give notice before release in some cases with an active immigration detainer. It also lets the attorney general or an affected person sue to enforce the rules and seek damages or a court order.

MD-2026-SB805.s: The bill changes Maryland’s student loan debt tax credit. It would let the Maryland Higher Education Commission extend the time for some people to use the credit to pay student loans, and it would make people repay only the unused part of the credit if they do not use all of it in time. The credit is for qualified taxpayers with at least $20,000 in student loan debt and at least $5,000 still owed, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026, for tax years after December 31, 2025.

MD-2026-SB808.s: The law changes how health care providers apply to join an insurance carrier’s provider panel. It shortens notice and decision deadlines, requires notices to be sent by email or mail, adds a $500-a-day civil penalty for missed notices, and ends the ability to charge an application fee. It also changes how carriers update provider directories, affects certain nonparticipating provider payments, and expands limits on which providers carriers may place on a panel.

MD-2026-SB851.s: In Anne Arundel County, the local government may allow a property tax credit on real property in a Rural Legacy area if the owner has sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program. The credit would apply to county property tax. The law takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.

MD-2026-SB897.s: The law changes the alcohol license cap in Cecil County. It raises the rule for Class A licenses to one license for every 1,200 registered voters, and says each election district must have at least two Class A licenses. It takes effect July 1, 2026.

MD-2026-SB974.s: The law changes who can serve as inspector for the Caroline County Board of License Commissioners. It says the inspector is either the county codes administrator or someone the board appoints. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.
